title: Independence & Conditional Independence
interviewAnswer: Independence means the joint factorizes into marginals; conditional independence means two variables become independent after conditioning on a third set. Conditional independence is central to graphical models and causal reasoning.
keyPoints: Zero correlation does not generally imply independence.
Conditioning can remove or create dependence.
DAG separation statements are about conditional independence.
why: Independence & Conditional Independence is a recurring foundation across data science and machine learning because it affects both theoretical correctness and practical system behavior.
intuition: Zero correlation does not generally imply independence.
deepDive: Independence means the joint factorizes into marginals; conditional independence means two variables become independent after conditioning on a third set. Conditional independence is central to graphical models and causal reasoning. Conditioning can remove or create dependence. DAG separation statements are about conditional independence. The interview-level skill is not merely recalling the definition: explain the assumptions, what diagnostic evidence you would inspect, and what alternative you would choose when those assumptions fail.
workedExample: Two symptoms may be dependent overall but independent after conditioning on their common disease cause.
commonMistakes: Using the concept mechanically without checking assumptions or data semantics.
Reporting one metric/result without examining uncertainty, slices or failure modes.
followUps: What assumptions or limitations does Independence & Conditional Independence have?
How would you validate Independence & Conditional Independence on a real dataset?
production: In production, make assumptions explicit, validate on representative slices, compare with a simple baseline and monitor the signals that can drift.
